summary: Independently verified 134E.5's Rendering Architecture implementation via fresh adversarial probing, rather than trusting its report, documentation, or its own 97/98 tests. Found and repaired one genuine BLOCKING defect in src/pcae/core/rendering.py, discovered by direct adversarial probing before any new test was written: undisclosed unresolved content in rendered prose. When a primary category's value could not be resolved from the source, Markdown/plain-text output still printed the category's structural classifications line (e.g. blocking) with no inline disclosure that the corresponding finding/repair body was unavailable -- the structured RenderingResult.diagnostics/content_preserved/completeness already correctly flagged the gap, but the rendered text itself did not. Repaired by adding an explicit [content unresolved: source value unavailable] line inline wherever this occurs, applying uniformly across all four affected prose renderers via the shared _resolve_section_lines() helper. Independently re-derived and confirmed the dual-input render(view, source, renderer_id) contract is necessary (views carry no content values), safe (digest check transitively rejects wrong-profile/wrong-phase/forged sources -- profile_id is embedded in ExtractionResult.compute_digest()), and contract-consistent. 42 new fresh adversarial tests covering all 40 required probe areas plus 2 authority-boundary re-confirmations, plus the original 97/98 tests (140 combined), pass; 1264 combined regression tests pass; fast_green 4390/4390 passing this run. No new NON-BLOCKING observations recorded; the three carried forward from prior phases remain open, none proven genuinely BLOCKING for Rendering specifically. The module remains isolated, disconnected lifecycle authority. 134E.6 not begun.
